brief: Global bond yields have risen sharply year-to-date on stronger nominal growth, lingering inflation, fiscal concerns and AI-related debt issuance crowding out capital; despite the sell-off, the 10-year yield near 5% is close to its 250-year average of 4.7%, so yields are higher but not historically high. GS frames the optimal bond weight via Modern Portfolio Theory: relative return, relative risk, diversification benefit and the return on cash. Near-term, energy prices and central bank policy drive both assets, with sharp yield spikes weighing more on equities; GS is tactically Neutral over 3 months. Over 12 months it stays OW equities, N bonds, UW credit, since resilient earnings still favor equities, though materially slower growth or a fading AI earnings tailwind would strengthen the bond case. Longer term, higher starting yields should lift strategic bond allocations toward the 35-55% historical range, without a full return to 60/40. For hedging, GS favors front-end receiver swaptions for recession convexity and TLT puts for duration risk, plus diversification via low-volatility/high-dividend equities and convertibles.
